subject: Coordinating live demo windows across US / EU / APAC — FinLeaf
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@finleaf.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: devops@finleaf.com
Date: Sun, 30 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Live demo request — three-region coverage

Hi Marcus,

We're ready to move forward with a product demo for the engineering and security teams. Key ask: run one live session that covers US, EMEA, and APAC stakeholders. We're aware the upcoming DST changes make the window narrow — EU switches later than the US next week which complicates overlap windows.

Can you propose a few 60-minute windows (UTC preferred) that account for the DST mismatch? We have engineers in London (UTC+0/UTC+1 after EU DST), NYC (EDT), and Bangalore (IST) and would prefer a live Q&A for APAC.

Thanks — attaching rough availability on our side (see attached).

Priya Sharma
Head of Integrations, FinLeaf
priya.sharma@finleaf.com

Attachments: finleaf_availability.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@finleaf.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Mar 2025 09:35:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Live demo request — three-region coverage

Hi Priya — thanks for the context and the availability sheet. I'm copying Olga (EMEA lead) and Mina (APAC coverage) so we can land a time that works globally.

I attached a short ICS with candidate slots and a simple timezone_matrix.csv that shows conversions across the three regions taking into account the upcoming DST offsets. Quick notes:
- US Spring forward occurs on 2025-03-09; EU moves a week later on 2025-03-16 in many countries — in our target week that creates a one-week period with different offsets.
- To maximize overlap and keep the APAC live Q&A, my proposals (all 60 min):
  1) 14:00–15:00 UTC (US: 10:00 EDT, EMEA: 14:00 BST/15:00 CEST depending on location, APAC: 19:30 IST)
  2) 15:30–16:30 UTC (US: 11:30 EDT, EMEA: 16:30 CET, APAC: 21:00 IST) — later for APAC but still feasible for live Q&A if you can keep <30% of attendees in APAC
  3) 20:00–21:00 UTC fallback (US late, EMEA evening, APAC morning) — we only recommend this if APAC priority is highest.

If you pick one, we'll send calendar invites with timezone conversions shown and record the session. If APAC needs a dedicated live slot, we can offer a short follow-up 30-minute session for them.

Attaching: candidate_slots.ics, timezone_matrix.csv, finleaf_sdr_notes.pdf

Cheers,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
Attachment: candidate_slots.ics
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@finleaf.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Mar 2025 09:48:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Live demo request — three-region coverage

Thanks Marcus — I reviewed the matrix. Two small operational asks from EMEA side:
- For UK participants we should show both GMT and BST labels in the invite text during the transition week to avoid confusion.
- Can we avoid proposing 20:00–21:00 UTC if more than 10 EMEA people will attend (that pushes into late evening for many).

Priya — from FinLeaf's attachment I see strong preference for the afternoon UTC window. If 14:00–15:00 UTC works for you I'll prepare the slide deck and include a 5-minute security architecture callout up front.

Olga
Regional Solutions Lead, EMEA | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
